newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus rises on international outlook.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus rises on international outlook.

text.p: Shares in French pay-television station Canal Plus jumped six percent on Thursday as hopes grew for successful outcomes to talks in Germany and Spain, analysts said.

Canal Plus posted on Wednesday 1996 net attributable profit in line with estimates at 741 million francs. The rise in the stock price represented a catch-up as the share has lost 1.57 percent since the start of the year.
The stock was up six percent at 1,131 francs at 1505 GMT, while the market was down 1.24 percent on the last day of the monthly account.

Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure gave a presentation to analysts on Thursday morning. Company executives confirmed that the integration of Nethold would hit this year's profits but a near-breakeven result was expected.
"But the main thing was that they (Canal Plus) said they were on the point of sorting out their differences in Germany and Spain. That has reassured the market," said an analyst.
Canal Plus believed a compromise was possible this year in Germany with media mogul Leo Kirch, the Bertelsmann group and Deutsche Telekom on developing digital television.
Lescure also said an agreement was probable in the next few weeks in Spain on a digital service and ruled out the possibility of giving up a majority holding in CanalSatellite Digital.

Analysts also pointed to the healthy development of CanalSatellite in France, which has set a target of 650,000 subscribers by the end of 1997, of which 500,000 are expected to be customers for the digital service. Turnover is forecast to be one billion francs.
